decks.summary: Core Set Wendy built on two-card combos: her Amulet replays Lucky! and Backstab, Scavenging recovers items and Leo De Luca adds actions; the first step of a cycle-by-cycle series.
The Revised Core Wendy rebuilt as an evasive cluever: Leo De Luca on turn one, Flashlight and "Look what I found!" for clues, Pickpocketing and Cunning Distraction to slip enemies; not for solo.
Two-core-set Wendy sharing a collection with four sibling decks: she evades with Elusive and Pickpocketing, strikes with Sneak Attack, and finds clues with Flashlight and "Look what I found!".

Advanced-Amulet Wendy who replays events from her discard pile, covers five classes for Cheat the System and Strength in Numbers, and passes almost any test; complex, flexible, and generous with Black Market.
Dunwich-era Wendy heading for Will to Survive, with Lone Wolf and Fine Clothes, Fire Axe for cheap kills, and Double or Nothing to double her best events.

Daredevil Darling updated for The Scarlet Keys: Salvage replays items, Makeshift Trap and Friends in Low Places add customizable events, and Talisman of Protection with Pocket Telescope covers classes for Cheat the System.
Carcosa-era Wendy still built toward Will to Survive, adding Fight or Flight to power Backstab and Fire Axe, and Quick Thinking and Resourceful for tempo.

Solo Expert Wendy tuned for Carcosa's Curtain Call: Baseball Bat and Backstab with Double or Nothing for burst damage, Leo De Luca and Lone Wolf for tempo and money, Fine Clothes for the campaign's tests.
Original-Amulet Wendy who dual-wields Lockpicks for clues and orders her events so the Amulet replays Nothing Left to Lose, Black Market and Easy Mark from the top of her discard pile.
Solo Hard Night of the Zealot combo Wendy: Leo De Luca, Will to Survive, Backstab and Double or Nothing aim to kill Umôrdhoth in a single turn, with the Amulet reusing the pieces.
